A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Inductive Moment Matching by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet generation results, training-stability experiments, scaling studies, and ablations in Section 7 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v7 retains these original experiments and adds ImageNet results for 10, 16, and 32 sampling steps in Appendix I.4 and Table 6.

M1.justification: The written method specification receives local corrections: Section 4.2 changes kernel scaling from 1/c_out(s,t) to 1/|c_out(s,t)|, and Appendix C.6 corrects subtraction to addition in the alternative reciprocal-noise mapping. The architecture, inductive training framework, and sampling algorithms remain the same; these edits do not establish that implementations changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate unconditional CIFAR-10 and class-conditional ImageNet-256×256 generation. Additional sampling steps retain the same datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds U-ViT-H (Bao et al., 2023) to the ImageNet comparison, reporting FID 2.29, 50 steps, and 501M parameters. The existing comparator membership is otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Appendix I.4 extends ImageNet evaluation beyond the earlier eight-step maximum to 10, 16, and 32 steps, with guidance weight 1.5. Existing training settings, model configurations, preprocessing, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Appendix I.4 explicitly investigates where inference-time scaling saturates, extending the earlier analysis through 32 steps. Existing embedding, particle-count, sampler, parameterization, weighting, and precision ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point FID values and convergence curves without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports ImageNet FIDs of 1.98, 1.90, and 1.89 at 10, 16, and 32 steps with guidance 1.5. Table 2 also adds U-ViT-H's 2.29 result. Existing scores, including IMM's eight-step 1.99 and CIFAR-10 two-step 1.98, are unchanged; the new lower scores use larger sampling budgets.

T1.justification: Appendices B.3–B.4 correct the invertibility threshold and induction endpoint involving c0(s). Lemma 1 and Appendix G.1 correct the kernel sign and diagonal value from 1 to 0, removing the spurious additive constant. Appendix C.9 also corrects the gradient-scaling expression. These refine existing derivations without adding new theorems.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: stable training from scratch, distributional convergence, connections to prior methods, and the headline CIFAR-10 and ImageNet results. Additional longer-step evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v7 adds the interpretation that performance largely saturates beyond 16 steps and expands Appendix G.1's critique of the consistency-model objective as a distributional divergence. Section 7.1 replaces the MAR 10× speedup assertion with discussion of inference scaling and the new comparison against 2B-parameter VAR.

D1.justification: Equation 67 corrects the empirical-loss weighting from w(s_i,t_j) to w(s_i,t_i), clarifying computation within particle groups. Other implementation formulas receive local corrections. Table 5, latent preprocessing, precision recommendations, and VAE access information are retained.

R1.justification: v7 adds Bao et al. (2023) and its U-ViT baseline, and sharpens the discussion of consistency models in Appendix G.1. The broader positioning relative to diffusion, distillation, GANs, and generative moment matching remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits comprise localized paragraph revisions, typo corrections, explicit algorithm cross-references, publication information, and the insertion of Appendix I.4 with subsequent subsection renumbering. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v7 adds Table 6 and a U-ViT-H row in Table 2. Earlier appendix Tables 6–7 become Tables 7–8 and are arranged alongside the new table; Algorithm 4 also moves between pages. Existing figures and sample grids are preserved.

improvement.justification: Corrections to Lemma 1 and the convergence argument improve mathematical accuracy, while the new sampling study provides useful evidence about performance saturation. These are limited gains over an otherwise stable study. One correction remains incompletely propagated: Section 4.2 uses 1/|c_out|, but Appendix C.8 still specifies 1/c_out.
